Initial running
Initial findings using fasta - Fasta: found only 38 IS [4 unique IS] - Suspected because there only 3 contigs and eris used those long contigs to analyse the data - More IS found using GFA

title: Eris Meeting
text:
Fragmentation
When I looked at the data, I found that the assembly graph are more fragmented compared to the fasta file. That is why I fragmented it.
In result: More IS found after fragmentation

Simulated (gfa)

paf_cols = [
    "query_name", "query_length", "query_start", "query_end", "strand",
    "target_name", "target_length", "target_start", "target_end",
    "num_matches", "alignment_length", "mapq"
]

# PAF has no header row and is tab-separated; extra tag columns (tp:A:P, cm:i:..., etc.)
paf_df = pd.read_csv(
    "../result/aft_sort/sim_gfa/aln_gfa.paf",
    sep="\t",
    header=None,
    usecols=range(12),
    names=paf_cols
)

# Extract just the real-genome (target) position info
gfa_pred = paf_df[["query_name", "target_name", "target_start", "target_end", "strand"]]

# ---

sim_gfa = pd.read_csv("../result/aft_sort/sim_gfa/eris_new_gfa_sim_report.tsv", sep="\t")

clean_gfa = sim_gfa.iloc[:,:3]

# Extract the name
clean_gfa["name"] = clean_gfa["target"].str.split("_").str[0]
clean_gfa["repeats"] = clean_gfa.groupby("name")["locus_id"].transform(lambda x: pd.factorize(x)[0] + 1)

# clean_gfa = clean_gfa.drop(columns=["gene_id", "locus_id", "target"])
print(clean_gfa)

# Match the location
print(gfa_pred.head(10))

# How many unique locus in total based on their strand
strand_counts = gfa_pred.groupby("query_name")["strand"].value_counts().unstack(fill_value=0)

gfa_loc = gfa_pred.copy()

print(gfa_loc[gfa_loc["query_name"] == "locus_split_419597b9"])
